rationale: B is better because it targets long-span verbatim repetition more precisely, distinguishes soft penalties from hard blocking, and connects detection to adaptive sampling, retry, and serving controls. Its rankings are more actionable and generally better aligned with effectiveness-versus-test-cost tradeoffs. It does overstate how easy high-quality DPO pair construction is and underspecifies how a decoder would penalize the first token of a future matching span, but A has more consequential weaknesses, especially its inaccurate claim that a diverse speculative proposer changes an exact verifier’s output behavior and its comparatively blunt short n-gram bans and temperature recommendation.
